algorithm.Title: Burns - Chemical - Female (Child)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Child | Female
Definition: UAT-only emergency recognition and decontamination pathway for suspected chemical exposure causing a skin or eye burn; not approved for real-patient or production use.

Background.ExpertReviewer: Pending qualified Qatar adult, pediatric, burns, ophthalmology, toxicology, and HazMat review

FirstAid: Call Qatar 999 immediately and follow the operator's instructions. Do not enter a contaminated area or touch the chemical without suitable protection. Move away from fumes only if this can be done safely. Using gloves or another protective barrier, carefully cut away contaminated clothing rather than pulling it over the head; do not remove material stuck to skin. Brush visible dry powder away without spreading it or exposing the responder. Unless the product label, safety data sheet, or 999 operator specifically warns that water is unsafe for that substance, immediately irrigate affected skin or eyes with copious cool or lukewarm running water for about 1 hour. Let runoff flow away from unaffected skin and the other eye. Remove contact lenses only if easy and continue irrigation. Do not scrub, rub, neutralize with another chemical, apply cream, ointment, ice, or medicine, or delay irrigation while identifying the product. Keep the container or a photograph available for emergency responders if safe. Do not drive the patient to hospital. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.

questions.Question: Was the burn caused only by heat, flame, hot liquid, or steam, with no chemical or acid exposure?
questions.Information: A heat-only burn belongs in the Burns - Thermal pathway. Any chemical or acid exposure remains here.

questions.Question: Has a harmful acid, alkali, cleaning product, industrial chemical, or unknown chemical contacted the skin or eyes, or caused pain, burning, visible injury, breathing symptoms, or reduced responsiveness? If the substance or exposure type is uncertain, keep this emergency disposition and do not redirect to a combined or lower-acuity burn pathway.
questions.Information: NHS.UK treats acid or chemical exposure to skin or eyes as an emergency requiring immediate first aid and hospital assessment. Uncertainty must fail closed because chemical identity changes decontamination risks.

advice.Title: Chemical exposure — call Qatar 999

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: Is the scene safe to approach without exposing the caller or responder to fumes, liquid, powder, contaminated clothing, fire, or another hazard?
initialAssessmentQuestions.Rationale: Condition-relevant source assessment retained from the Batch 5 source protocol.

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: What is the patient's exact age, what product or chemical was involved, and is the label or safety data sheet available without delaying first aid?
initialAssessmentQuestions.Rationale: Condition-relevant source assessment retained from the Batch 5 source protocol.

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: Did the chemical contact the skin, eyes, face, mouth, airway, or clothing, and how large is the affected area?
initialAssessmentQuestions.Rationale: Condition-relevant source assessment retained from the Batch 5 source protocol.

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: Is there breathing difficulty, coughing, choking, collapse, reduced responsiveness, severe eye pain, or vision change?
initialAssessmentQuestions.Rationale: Condition-relevant source assessment retained from the Batch 5 source protocol.

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: Has contaminated clothing been removed safely, has any dry chemical been brushed away, and has appropriate irrigation started?
initialAssessmentQuestions.Rationale: Condition-relevant source assessment retained from the Batch 5 source protocol.

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: What change has a safe parent or caregiver observed in alertness, breathing, eating or drinking, sleep, play, and normal activity?
initialAssessmentQuestions.Rationale: Child assessment includes safe-caregiver observation; it does not create a different clinical threshold.
